note: [L] never states the infinite sum equals the Euler product; it proves a lower bound for the truncated sum over q<=r_0 (Sum_{Qset} coefN >= 1.314) using the product over odd primes <=r_0 with a Rankin tail. Note a_p = -1/(p-1)^2 for p|N and 1/(p-1)^3 otherwise, so 1+a_p matches the displayed factors.

snippet.text:
/-- `μ(q) c_q(N)/φ(q)³ = ∏_{p∣q} a_p(N)` for squarefree `q`, `0` otherwise. -/
noncomputable def coefN (N q : ℕ) : ℝ := if Squarefree q then ∏ p ∈ q.primeFactors, aP N p else 0

proof_context.conclusion: $\mathrm{coefN}(N,q)=\prod_{p|q}a_p(N)$ for squarefree $q$ (0 otherwise), $a_p=(1-[p|N]p)/(p-1)^3$; for squarefree $q$ equals $\phi((q,N))\mu((q,N))/\phi(q)^3$.
